_help: Web3 Hall of Famers: the 50 people, from web3_people_game_list.xlsx. Facts are public information as of 5 Nov 2026 and need checking before launch (entries with check say what to look at). level: easy, medium or hard. anon: no known face (a hooded drawing shows). caution: shown as a cautionary tale, not a role model; keep the wording factual. Portraits: put a drawing at images/people/ID.webp (square, 600 by 600) and it shows by itself; until then a sketch with initials shows. x: their X (Twitter) handle without @, used to tag them in share posts; CHECK EVERY HANDLE before posting (left out for Satoshi, people with no public account, Hal Finney who passed away in 2014, and the cautionary tales, who are never tagged). more: the Read more link. story: two or three sentences told on their card and page. known: what they are known for (short).

people.name: Satoshi Nakamoto
people.why: Published the Bitcoin whitepaper in 2008 and launched the network in January 2009
people.fun: Real identity has never been confirmed
people.story: In October 2008 someone calling themselves Satoshi Nakamoto shared a 9-page paper describing digital cash with no bank in the middle. They mined Bitcoin's first block in January 2009, worked with early developers by email and forum posts, then went quiet in 2011 and handed the project to others.

people.name: Vitalik Buterin
people.why: Proposed a blockchain that runs programs (smart contracts), not just payments
people.fun: Was 19 when he published the Ethereum whitepaper in 2013
people.story: Vitalik co-founded Bitcoin Magazine as a teenager. In 2013 he wrote the Ethereum whitepaper, and Ethereum went live in 2015. He then pushed its switch from mining to proof of stake, which happened in 2022 and is known as The Merge.
known: The Merge to proof of stake (2022)

people.name: Gavin Wood
people.role: Cofounder of Ethereum, founder of Polkadot
people.why: Wrote the technical specification for Ethereum and coined the term Web3
people.fun: Proposed Solidity, the language used for most Ethereum smart contracts
people.story: Gavin was Ethereum's first CTO and wrote its Yellow Paper, the exact technical rules every Ethereum client follows. He left to found Parity Technologies and then Polkadot, a network built to connect many blockchains. In 2014 he described his vision as Web 3.0.

people.name: Anatoly Yakovenko
people.why: Invented Proof of History, which timestamps transactions to speed up the chain
people.fun: Previously worked at Qualcomm
people.story: Anatoly spent more than a decade as an engineer at Qualcomm. In 2017 he wrote the Solana whitepaper around one idea: a clock built into the chain so computers agree on time faster. Solana went live in 2020 and became known for quick, cheap transactions.

people.name: Raj Gokal
people.why: Helped build the company and ecosystem around Solana
people.fun: Solana is named after Solana Beach, a surf town in California
people.story: Raj joined Anatoly early and co-founded Solana Labs in 2018. While Anatoly led the technology, Raj focused on the company, funding and the apps and community growing around Solana.

people.name: Charles Hoskinson
people.role: Cofounder of Ethereum, founder of Cardano
people.why: Built Cardano with a research first, peer reviewed approach
people.fun: Was part of Ethereum's original founding team before leaving in 2014
people.story: Charles was one of Ethereum's eight cofounders before leaving in 2014. He then co-founded IOHK (now Input Output) and built Cardano, which bases its design on peer-reviewed research papers. Cardano launched in 2017.

people.name: Changpeng Zhao (CZ)
people.why: Built the world's largest crypto exchange by trading volume
people.fun: Launched Binance in 2017 and stepped down as CEO in 2023 as part of a US settlement
people.check: Check legal wording and any later updates before launch.
people.story: CZ wrote trading software before crypto. He launched Binance in 2017 and within months it was the biggest exchange by trading volume. In 2023 he stepped down as CEO and pleaded guilty in the US to failing to keep an effective anti-money laundering program, and served a four-month sentence in 2024.

people.name: Justin Sun
people.why: Built Tron, a chain heavily used for USDT transfers
people.fun: Bought the banana artwork Comedian for 6.2 million dollars in 2024
people.story: Justin founded Tron in 2017 and bought BitTorrent, the file sharing company, in 2018. Tron became one of the main networks people use to send USDT cheaply.

people.name: Sandeep Nailwal
people.why: Helped scale Ethereum and is one of the best known India born crypto founders
people.fun: Polygon began as Matic Network in 2017 and rebranded in 2021
people.story: Sandeep co-founded Matic Network in 2017 with fellow Indian founders Jaynti Kanani and Anurag Arjun, to make Ethereum faster and cheaper to use. It became Polygon in 2021. That year he also started the Crypto Covid Relief Fund for India.
known: Crypto Covid Relief Fund for India (2021)

people.name: Illia Polosukhin
people.why: Combines AI and blockchain in one ecosystem
people.fun: Coauthored Attention Is All You Need, the paper that introduced the Transformer behind modern AI
people.story: Before crypto, Illia worked on AI at Google and co-wrote the 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer. He co-founded NEAR in 2018, first as an AI project, then as a blockchain designed to be easy to use.

people.name: Hal Finney
people.why: Received the first Bitcoin transaction ever sent by Satoshi
people.fun: Posted the words Running bitcoin on January 11, 2009
people.story: Hal was a cryptographer who worked on PGP, the email encryption program. In 2004 he built reusable proof of work, an early digital token. He was one of the first people to run Bitcoin and got its first transaction from Satoshi in 2009. He later lived with ALS and passed away in 2014.

people.name: Nick Szabo
people.why: Coined the idea of smart contracts and designed Bit Gold, a Bitcoin precursor
people.fun: Some people speculate he is Satoshi, which he denies
people.story: In the 1990s Nick described smart contracts: deals enforced by code, using a vending machine as his example. His Bit Gold design, written up between 1998 and 2005, is seen as a forerunner of Bitcoin.

people.name: Adam Back
people.why: His Hashcash proof of work idea is cited in the Bitcoin whitepaper
people.fun: Was one of the first people Satoshi emailed
people.story: In 1997 Adam invented Hashcash, a way to fight email spam by making every message cost a little computing work. That proof of work idea became the heart of Bitcoin mining. He co-founded Blockstream in 2014.

people.name: David Chaum
people.why: Created DigiCash, an early private digital money system
people.fun: Invented blind signatures, the cryptography behind early private payments
people.story: In the early 1980s David showed how payments could be private using blind signatures. He founded DigiCash in 1989 to build ecash, many years before Bitcoin. DigiCash went bankrupt in 1998, but its ideas shaped digital money.

people.name: Brian Armstrong
people.why: Took crypto to public markets when Coinbase listed in 2021
people.fun: Coinbase listed directly on Nasdaq in April 2021
people.story: Brian worked at Airbnb before founding Coinbase in 2012 to make buying Bitcoin simple. Coinbase grew into the largest US exchange, listed on Nasdaq in April 2021 and later built Base, its own layer 2 network.

people.name: Emilie Choi
people.why: Runs operations and acquisitions at the largest US exchange
people.fun: Joined Coinbase from LinkedIn in 2018
people.story: Emilie led corporate development at LinkedIn before joining Coinbase in 2018. There she ran its deals and acquisitions and later became President and COO.

people.name: Yi He
people.role: Cofounder and joint CEO of Binance
people.why: Marketing and growth leader behind Binance's global reach
people.fun: Was named joint CEO of Binance in December 2025
people.check: Joint CEO role (Dec 2025): check before launch.
people.story: Yi He co-founded Binance in 2017 and led its marketing as it spread across many countries. She also led Binance Labs, the company's investment arm.

people.name: Paolo Ardoino
people.why: Runs the issuer of USDT, the most traded stablecoin
people.fun: Was previously the CTO of Bitfinex
people.story: Paolo was a software developer who became CTO of Bitfinex and Tether, then Tether's CEO in 2023. Tether issues USDT, the most traded stablecoin.

people.name: Jeremy Allaire
people.why: Issues USDC, one of the biggest dollar stablecoins
people.fun: Circle listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 2025
people.story: Jeremy built web companies including Allaire (maker of ColdFusion) and Brightcove before founding Circle in 2013. In 2018 Circle and Coinbase launched USDC, a dollar stablecoin backed by cash and short-term US government debt.

people.name: Brad Garlinghouse
people.why: Led Ripple through its long legal fight with the SEC over XRP
people.fun: The SEC case began in December 2020 and ran until 2025
people.story: Brad was an executive at Yahoo and AOL before joining Ripple in 2015 and becoming CEO in 2017. Ripple builds payment tools for banks and supports the XRP Ledger.
known: The XRP case against the SEC

people.name: Hayden Adams
people.why: Created the automated market maker that lets anyone swap tokens without an order book
people.fun: Built the first version after being laid off from an engineering job at Siemens
people.story: After being laid off in 2017, Hayden taught himself to code Ethereum smart contracts on a friend's suggestion. He launched Uniswap in November 2018: a pool of two tokens that anyone can swap against, with no order book.

people.name: Stani Kulechov
people.why: Built one of the largest decentralized lending protocols
people.fun: Started in 2017 as ETHLend before becoming Aave
people.story: Stani started ETHLend in 2017 while studying law in Finland. It became Aave in 2018 (aave means ghost in Finnish) and introduced flash loans: loans borrowed and paid back inside one single transaction.

people.name: Rune Christensen
people.why: Created DAI, a decentralized dollar stablecoin
people.fun: DAI launched in 2017 and was one of the first decentralized stablecoins
people.story: Rune founded MakerDAO in 2014 to build a stablecoin with no company holding the dollars. DAI launched in 2017, kept near one dollar by crypto locked up as collateral. Maker rebranded to Sky in 2024.

people.name: Sergey Nazarov
people.why: Chainlink brings real world data onto blockchains
people.fun: Chainlink's fan community calls itself the LINK Marines
people.story: Sergey co-founded Chainlink, which published its whitepaper in 2017. Chainlink oracles bring prices and other outside data onto blockchains, and most DeFi apps rely on data like that.

people.name: Andre Cronje
people.why: Helped kick off DeFi summer in 2020
people.fun: Launched the YFI token with no premine, giving all tokens to users
people.story: Andre, a South African developer, launched Yearn Finance in 2020. It moved deposits between DeFi apps to chase the best yield, and its YFI token had no team allocation, which helped spark DeFi summer. He is also linked with the Fantom chain, now Sonic.

people.name: Jesse Pollak
people.why: Builds Base, a popular Ethereum layer 2
people.fun: Base launched in 2023
people.story: Jesse leads Base at Coinbase. Base is a layer 2 network on Ethereum that opened to everyone in August 2023 to make onchain apps cheap and simple, kicked off with an event called Onchain Summer.

people.name: Meow
people.why: Built Jupiter, Solana's leading swap aggregator
people.fun: Operates under a pseudonym
people.story: Meow, the pseudonymous cofounder of Jupiter, built Solana's main swap aggregator, which searches many exchanges for the best price. Jupiter launched its JUP token with a large airdrop in January 2024.

people.name: Michael Saylor
people.why: Pioneered public companies holding Bitcoin as a treasury asset
people.fun: Strategy started buying Bitcoin in August 2020
people.story: Michael co-founded MicroStrategy (now called Strategy) in 1989. In August 2020 the company began turning its cash into Bitcoin and kept buying, becoming the largest company holder of Bitcoin.

people.name: Larry Fink
people.why: His firm's Bitcoin ETF brought traditional finance into crypto
people.fun: Called Bitcoin an index of money laundering in 2017 and later became a supporter
people.story: Larry co-founded BlackRock in 1988, now the world's largest asset manager. In January 2024 its spot Bitcoin ETF, IBIT, began trading in the US and quickly became one of the biggest Bitcoin funds.

people.name: Cathie Wood
people.why: Early institutional voice for Bitcoin and Ethereum
people.fun: Known for bold long term price predictions
people.story: Cathie founded ARK Invest in 2014 to invest in fast-changing technology. ARK was an early big fund manager to back Bitcoin, and in 2024 it launched a spot Bitcoin ETF with 21Shares.

people.name: Chris Dixon
people.why: Led one of the biggest crypto venture funds
people.fun: Popularized the phrase read, write, own to describe web eras
people.story: An early internet founder and investor, Chris launched a16z crypto at Andreessen Horowitz in 2018. In 2024 he published the book Read Write Own about why blockchains matter.

people.name: Meltem Demirors
people.why: Investor and speaker on digital assets
people.fun: Previously chief strategy officer at CoinShares
people.story: Meltem became a well known speaker and investor in digital assets. She was chief strategy officer at CoinShares, one of the early crypto investment firms, before founding Crucible Capital.

people.name: Mike Novogratz
people.why: Wall Street veteran who built a crypto financial services firm
people.fun: Was a hedge fund manager before turning to crypto
people.story: Mike was a partner at Goldman Sachs and ran a big hedge fund before he started buying Bitcoin around 2013. He founded Galaxy Digital in 2018 to offer trading, investing and other crypto services.

people.name: Arthur Hayes
people.why: Popularized perpetual futures, contracts with no expiry date
people.fun: BitMEX's perpetual swap became the model for most crypto derivatives
people.story: Arthur co-founded BitMEX in 2014. Its perpetual swap, launched in 2016, let traders bet on prices with no expiry date, and most crypto exchanges copied it. He left BitMEX in 2020 and now writes long essays on money and markets that many traders follow.

people.name: Paul Atkins
people.why: Leads the SEC with a friendlier approach to crypto since April 2025
people.fun: Sworn in as chair on April 21, 2025
people.check: Current role and Project Crypto: check before launch.
people.story: Paul was an SEC commissioner from 2002 to 2008. He returned as SEC Chair in April 2025 and launched Project Crypto to write clearer rules for digital assets.

people.name: Hester Peirce
people.why: Known as Crypto Mom for leading the SEC crypto task force
people.fun: Resigned from the SEC effective October 2, 2026
people.story: Hester joined the SEC as a commissioner in 2018. She often spoke out against crypto crackdowns, proposed a safe harbor to give new token projects time to grow, and in 2025 led the SEC's crypto task force.

people.name: Gary Gensler
people.why: Led the enforcement heavy era from 2021 to January 2025
people.fun: Taught a blockchain course at MIT before becoming SEC Chair
people.story: Gary was a Goldman Sachs partner, led the CFTC from 2009 to 2014 and taught at MIT. As SEC Chair from 2021 to January 2025 he brought many cases against crypto firms, arguing most tokens were securities. Spot Bitcoin ETFs were approved in January 2024, while he was Chair.

people.name: Caitlin Long
people.why: Pushes for crypto native banking
people.fun: Former Wall Street banker at Morgan Stanley
people.story: Caitlin spent over 20 years on Wall Street, then helped Wyoming pass crypto-friendly laws from 2017. In 2020 she founded Custodia Bank, first called Avanti, to bank crypto businesses.

people.name: Nayib Bukele
people.why: His country made Bitcoin legal tender in 2021
people.fun: El Salvador was the first country to do this
people.story: Nayib became president of El Salvador in 2019. In September 2021 his country made Bitcoin legal tender and launched the Chivo wallet. In 2025, as part of an IMF deal, the law changed so businesses no longer had to accept Bitcoin.
people.check: Check the 2025 law change wording before launch.

people.name: Andreas Antonopoulos
people.why: Wrote Mastering Bitcoin, a standard technical guide
people.fun: Known for talks that explain Bitcoin to non technical audiences
people.story: Andreas became one of Bitcoin's best known teachers through hundreds of free talks. His book Mastering Bitcoin (2014), and later Mastering Ethereum, are standard guides for developers.

people.name: Laura Shin
people.why: Author of The Cryptopians, a book on Ethereum's early years
people.fun: Reports on crypto through her long running Unchained podcast
people.story: A former senior editor at Forbes, Laura started the Unchained podcast in 2016. Her 2022 book The Cryptopians tells the story of Ethereum's early years and The DAO hack.

people.name: ZachXBT
people.why: Exposes scams, rug pulls and hacks
people.fun: Stays anonymous while tracing stolen funds
people.story: ZachXBT is a self-taught onchain detective. Every transaction on a public blockchain can be followed, and his threads use that to expose scams and track stolen funds, often helping victims and exchanges freeze money.

people.name: Anthony Pompliano
people.why: Explains crypto and Bitcoin to mainstream audiences
people.fun: Widely known as Pomp
people.story: Pomp served in the US Army and worked at Facebook before co-founding Morgan Creek Digital. He hosts The Pomp Podcast and writes a daily letter about Bitcoin and markets.

people.name: Raoul Pal
people.why: Macro investor who argues crypto follows global liquidity cycles
people.fun: Previously a hedge fund sales head at Goldman Sachs
people.story: Raoul ran a macro hedge fund and wrote research for big investors before co-founding Real Vision in 2014, a finance video channel. He argues crypto prices follow the global supply of money, an idea he calls the Everything Code.

people.name: Balaji Srinivasan
people.why: Wrote The Network State and served as Coinbase CTO
people.fun: Was a general partner at a16z
people.story: Balaji co-founded Earn.com, which Coinbase bought in 2018, and then became Coinbase's CTO. He was a general partner at a16z and in 2022 wrote The Network State, about online communities that grow into new countries.

people.name: Ben Goertzel
people.why: Helped popularize the term artificial general intelligence
people.fun: Was chief scientist at Hanson Robotics, the maker of the robot Sophia
people.story: Ben is an AI researcher who helped popularise the term artificial general intelligence. In 2017 he launched SingularityNET, a blockchain marketplace for AI services, which in 2024 joined others to form the Artificial Superintelligence Alliance.

people.name: Sreeram Kannan
people.why: Created restaking, which lets staked ETH secure other services
people.fun: Is a professor at the University of Washington
people.story: Sreeram ran a blockchain research lab at the University of Washington. He founded EigenLayer, which went live in 2023 and lets ETH stakers reuse their stake to secure other services, an idea called restaking.

people.name: Elon Musk
people.role: CEO of Tesla and owner of X
people.why: His posts have repeatedly moved the price of Dogecoin
people.fun: Dogecoin started in 2013 as a joke
people.story: Elon runs Tesla and SpaceX and owns X. In 2021 Tesla said it had bought 1.5 billion dollars of Bitcoin, and Elon's posts about Dogecoin have often moved its price, a reminder of how much hype can move crypto.

people.name: Sam Bankman-Fried
people.why: A lesson in risk: FTX collapsed in November 2022
people.fun: Was convicted of fraud in 2023
people.story: Sam founded the trading firm Alameda Research in 2017 and the exchange FTX in 2019. In November 2022 FTX collapsed after it came out that customer money had been used by Alameda. In 2024 he was sentenced to 25 years in prison. The lesson: keep only what you trade on any exchange.

people.name: Do Kwon
people.why: A lesson in algorithmic stablecoins: Terra and Luna collapsed in May 2022
people.fun: The collapse erased roughly 40 billion dollars in market value
people.check: Check for later legal updates (sentencing) before launch.
people.story: Do co-founded Terraform Labs in 2018. Its UST stablecoin tried to stay at one dollar through an algorithm tied to the LUNA token, not cash reserves. In May 2022 UST lost its peg and both tokens collapsed. He was later extradited to the US and pleaded guilty to fraud charges in 2025.
